meta.prompt_note: Extraction prompt version 12 (2026-09-30) is the one the app uses now. Versions 9 to 11 fix what the UI audit and the Ask benchmark found in the published readings: a to-do's action and consequence and a key fact's label came out in the letter's German, with its number formats ("Semesterbeitrag überweisen", "94.99 EUR", "03.09.2026"); a letter's explanation could say there was nothing to do when the rules engine times a choice (an objection, a special right to cancel); and three terms the ledger could not hold: the working day a rent is due on (§ 556b BGB), a cancellation that must arrive by a day of the month (the Deutschlandticket's "by the 10th") and a fixed-term job that may be ended by notice after probation. The model also names a high-stakes letter itself (`high_stakes_kind`, ADR 0010), which code then checks. Version 12 adds three more terms the ledger could not hold: a monthly payment's day of the month or last working day, a standing order as the person's own transfer, and a contract that names the statutory notice periods. Each version was checked on the dev split before the test split, but the test split was recorded four times for them, which is iteration on it: read the row with that in mind. Version 9 scored 54 of 56 (dev 24 of 25). Version 10 added the three terms and scored 53 of 56 (dev 23 of 25): it left the delivery date out of fines served by Zustellung ("zugestellt am") on both splits, so their objection deadlines were counted from an earlier day (versions 8 and 9 filled it in all 6 fines; version 10 in 4, one of them read as an explicit anchor, and left it out of 2). Version 11 says so explicitly, was checked on the dev split (24 of 25) and scored 54 of 56. In its 91 readings no key-fact label, action or consequence is in German and no prose field uses the letter's date or amount format; one names a high-stakes kind, correctly (a landlord's heating-cost statement, `operating_costs`). Its two misses are early, on the safe side: a questionnaire's "10 Arbeitstagen (Montag bis Freitag)" read as working days that include Saturdays, so its return date came out two days early (version 9 made the same slip on the letter's photo); and the tax notice above that prints a posting day two days after its own date: the old reading passed that day and the engine counted from the letter's date on purpose (a computing error by this page's taxonomy); this reading leaves the day out, so the engine counts from the letter's date anyway (a reading error): the same date. Version 12 was checked on the dev split (24 of 25) and scored 54 of 56, with the same two misses, both early, on the safe side: the questionnaire's ten working days, this time on the letter's photo (its text PDF was read right), and the tax notice, counted from the letter's date again. No benchmark letter states one of version 10's or version 12's terms; version 10's are measured on the demo and in the Ask benchmark. Recording cost $14.18 (API-equivalent): version 9 $3.56, version 10 $3.51, version 11 $3.59, version 12 $3.51. Cost and latency per letter were measured on a different day from the published run and are not a comparison of the prompts. On 30 September the account lost access to Sonnet 5.5, and the app moved to the pinned id claude-sonnet-5, the model of the published run (an alias such as sonnet moves with releases; the recordings were made with one model). Version 12 was then recorded again with Sonnet 5 on both splits, the fifth recording of the test split for versions 9 to 12: dev 24 of 25, test 55 of 56, no dangerously late date, the one miss early (a tax assessment's objection deadline counted from an earlier day). These are the runs the row shows; the Sonnet 5.5 runs stay in evals/results as the record of that iteration. The Sonnet 5 recording cost $6.46 (dev $1.76, test $4.70).

items.title: Demanded payment of €287.40 (suspected scam)
items.quote: Überweisen Sie den Gesamtbetrag innerhalb von 72 Stunden, spätestens bis 06.08.2026, ausschließlich auf folgendes Treuhandkonto: IBAN LT71 7300 0101 2345 6789, Kontoinhaber: A. Petrauskas, Verwendungszweck EC-DE-2026-481120.

spec.text: innerhalb von 72 Stunden, spätestens bis 06.08.2026

items.explanation: The date given is Thu 6 Aug 2026.

warnings: This has strong hallmarks of a fake debt-collection scam: the payment account is a Lithuanian IBAN held by a private individual (A. Petrauskas), not the German 'Lotto-Muster-Club' creditor, which is unusual for a legitimate collection agency.

The 72-hour deadline and threats of immediate account seizure, a SCHUFA entry and criminal prosecution 'without further notice' are high-pressure tactics; a German bank account can only be seized after a court judgment, not directly by a collection agency.
The claim that 'a Widerspruch (objection) is pointless and only causes further costs' is misleading — in Germany you always retain the right to dispute a debt collection claim.
The added collection and account fees (€84.00 + €24.00) are large relative to the claimed principal debt of €179.40, which is atypical of legitimate collection costs.

The sender is registered only abroad (Cyprus) with no German address, which is common in fraudulent debt-collection schemes targeting people in Germany; verify independently before paying or responding.
The instructions on how to object are unclear — get advice. If they are missing or wrong, a one-year period may apply (§ 356 Abs. 2 AO, § 58 Abs. 2 VwGO, § 66 Abs. 2 SGG).
